mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 9.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a severe labor market downturn that triggers policy interventions and investor anticipation of economic recovery, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE has been above 9.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based demand contraction, which triggers a market correction as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative correlation between the joint decline of HOUST and RSAFS and S&P 500 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY), the economy faces stagflation risks, causing equity markets to decline as investors shift to safe assets, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0 and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate exceeding 2.0% (computed from GDPC1) signals strong economic momentum that boosts corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 QoQ growth exceeds 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 5.0%), the economy is in an overheating phase that prompts aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0% and UNRATE < 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 jobs per month indicates a strengthening labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100,000 jobs.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 5% month-over-month, it signals a weakening in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST declines by more than 5% MoM.
